page: Amazon Web Services x8g.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs via AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz. The CPU topology features 1 thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing includes hardware AES instructions, though x86-specific vector extensions are absent due to the underlying ARM ISA. The instance incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an extensive memory density of 16.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local instance storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data, and network connectivity is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark testing highlights the instance's strengths in memory throughput and data decompression. In the PassMark memory suite, the system achieved a strong score of 2931.98, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated machines. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 14.48 GB/sec, also landing in the top 25%. In contrast, compute-intensive execution reveals lower relative performance: the PassMark CPU score registered at 3954.8 and PassMark encryption at 753.37, falling into weaker percentiles compared to high-frequency x86 compute equivalents. General integer and system throughput remain stable in the mid-tier, demonstrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 5876.0 and Redis SET throughput reaching 9.35 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16:1 enables dense in-memory allocations without over-provisioning compute resources. This architecture minimizes expenditures for RAM-hungry applications that do not require intensive floating-point or heavy vector calculations. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage and entry-level 2 Gbps network baseline represent operational tradeoffs to consider when sizing I/O-heavy pipelines. Consequently, the x8g.xlarge is primarily suited for in-memory caching solutions like Redis or Memcached, intermediate data processing, memory-bound database caching layers, and general enterprise microservices with substantial heap requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per core. The platform integrates 36 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware AES acceleration, though it lacks local storage and requires external volumes. Network bandwidth maintains a 2 Gbps baseline. Benchmark outcomes show top-quartile PassMark memory performance and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression, contrasted with weaker PassMark CPU and cryptographic compute scores. Yielding a high memory-to-core ratio, x8g.xlarge provides cost-effective resource utilization for workloads requiring large memory footprints without intense compute overhead, making it well matched for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and memory-intensive ETL operations.
